question: During the streamer's visit to Shenzhen, when watching the drone show at Shenzhen Bay, what shapes did the drone formations sequentially transform into? 1. A person playing AR; 2. A rapidly developing city; 3. A dragon slowly swimming upwards; 4. A face slowly emerging; 5. An eagle soaring with wings spread;

decisive_steps.what_happened: Single clip_qa call over the whole window returned answer 1->5->3->4->2, citing an 'air-guitar person' at ~316497s and 'eagle' at ~316500-505s, both placed before the dragon (~316510-650s).
submit_answer copies the clip_qa ordering verbatim without cross-checking against the event_steps/episodes text it had already pulled.

rollouts.failure_point: Visual sub-agent misread an early forming-drone frame (~316497-505s, still a scattered/coalescing blue shape, not yet the dragon) as a 'person playing air guitar' and an 'eagle', producing a wrong order (1,5,3,4,2) instead of the correct (3,5,1,4,2). The episodes DB text for that exact time window ('a massive formation of drones assembles ... forming a glowing blue shape', then 'sculpting a dragon') was never queried by this rollout, so there was no independent text evidence to catch the misread.
rollouts.evidence_checked: Pulled the source frame at 316498s myself: it shows drones still scattering/forming a vague blue cloud (plus a foreground quadcopter camera-drone silhouette) - not a discernible person or eagle shape. The dragon is clearly formed by 316510s.

rollouts.answer: dragon -> eagle/bird -> person with VR-headset/tech icons -> face -> city (matches reference order 3,5,1,4,2)

clip_qa nonetheless reported a 'person playing air guitar/instrument' at ~316498s (the same misread frame as rollout 0) and the agent used that ordering, also swapping city and face at the end (317070 city, 317099 face), contradicting both its own retrieved episodes text (skull/face ~317008-317038 before castle/city ~317038-317098) and the visual evidence.

rollouts.failure_point: The rollout had the correct disambiguating text evidence in context (from its own run_sql) but did not reconcile it against the clip_qa visual misread; it trusted the visual sub-agent's wrong reading of the pre-dragon forming frame as a person, and additionally mis-ordered face/city at the end, compounding two errors into the worst-scoring answer.
rollouts.evidence_checked: Same frame check as rollout 0 at 316498s (no person shape visible, just a forming amorphous blue cloud) plus episodes text confirming skull(face)-then-castle/building(city) order, opposite of what rollout 3 submitted.

rollouts.answer: dragon -> eagle/bird -> AR/VR person -> face -> city (matches reference order 3,5,1,4,2)

decisive_steps.what_happened: clip_qa over the full clue window (316400-317120) returned a detailed, internally consistent chronology: dragon(~316512-660) -> bridge/bird(~316860-890) -> AR/VR person + IoT diagram(~316918-936) -> face/skull(~316990-317016) -> castle/city(~317060-317090) -> text card(~317102+), correctly separating the person/AR formation from the earlier dragon-forming frames that tripped up rollouts 0 and 3.

db_evidence.notes: The 30sec-granularity episodes captions fully and accurately narrate the sequence in plain text: drones assemble a glowing blue shape (316468-498) -> sculpt a DRAGON (316498-828) -> transform into a BIRD (316828-888, matches 'eagle soaring with wings spread') -> show changing years/network+hand/'IoT' imagery (316888-978, the closest DB match to 'a person playing AR') -> a SKULL forms (317008-1038, matches 'a face slowly emerging') -> a futuristic CASTLE/building (317038-1098, matches 'a rapidly developing city') -> text card 'Shenzhen Bay Skylshow' (317098+). This textual order (dragon, bird, AR/IoT imagery, skull/face, city) matches the reference answer 3,5,1,4,2 exactly, confirming the reference answer is correct and was retrievable via SQL alone without any visual inspection. Two rollouts (1 and 3) actually pulled this exact episodes text into context; rollout 1 used it (or converging clip_qa evidence) to get the right order, rollout 3 ignored the conflict with its own clip_qa misread and got it wrong.

root_causes: Visual sub-agent (clip_qa) misreading an early, still-forming/ambiguous drone frame (~316497-505s, before the dragon fully resolves) as a 'person playing air guitar' or 'eagle' - this single misattribution alone explains rollouts 0 and 3's wrong orderings.

No cross-checking between retrieved SQL/episodes text evidence (which correctly and unambiguously narrates dragon->bird->IoT/person->skull/face->city) and the clip_qa visual answer when the two conflicted (rollout 3 had both pieces of evidence in context and still deferred to the wrong visual read).

Under-scoped clip_qa time window in rollout 2 (316468-316888) that excluded the back half of the clue interval, causing 3 of 5 required shapes to never be inspected at all rather than a misread of them.

Heavy reliance on a single clip_qa call per rollout with no verification pass or second sampling when the sub-agent's answer was internally uncertain or contradicted structured text evidence already retrieved.
what_worked: The 30sec episodes captions in the DB are a highly reliable, directly queryable source for this kind of sequential-shape question and by themselves resolve the ordering (rollouts that engaged with this text alongside clip_qa succeeded).

clip_qa windows that spanned the entire clue interval (316400-317120/317158) rather than a truncated sub-window let the sub-agent see all 5 formations and produce a complete, correctly-ordered answer (rollouts 1 and 4).
transferable_lessons: For 'sequence of N described shapes' questions, always pull the full 30sec-granularity episodes text across the whole clue interval via run_sql before or alongside clip_qa - it often narrates the exact sequence in prose and is more reliable than a single visual pass over ambiguous, rapidly-changing formations.

When clip_qa's answer conflicts with previously retrieved SQL/text evidence, treat that as a red flag requiring reconciliation (e.g. a second clip_qa call zoomed on the disputed timestamp) rather than defaulting to the visual sub-agent's read.

Scope clip_qa windows to cover the full total_intervals span for ordering/counting questions with multiple sub-events; a narrowed window risks silently dropping items instead of just mis-ordering them.

Be skeptical of shapes reported from the very start of a formation's transition (still-scattering drone clusters) - these frames are visually ambiguous and prone to being misclassified as an unrelated shape; prefer frames from the middle of a formation's dwell time.
open_questions: Whether the option 'a person playing AR' is meant to map to the DB's 'network+hand/IoT' formation (~316918-948) or to the 'triangular structure with spherical center' / 'real human, wondering if it's Taylor Swift' formation (~316978-1008) - both are plausible referents and the exact drone-formation image was not independently visually confirmed by this diagnosis.
